source.title: We Don't Need No Adam, All We Need Is EVE: On The Variance of Dual Learning Rate And Beyond

record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizer variants and reports training and validation metrics on natural-label image classification, bearing conceptually on optimizer-related generalization in V4; it does not test random-label memorization or the other claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports Adam and EVE training/validation metrics on two natural-image datasets. Rows record those optimizer comparisons. It does not report random-label training, train-test error gaps, or the other interventions and measurements in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study compares two adaptive optimizers, EVE and Adam. It never compares either with SGD or momentum SGD, so its results do not test V4's relative generalization claim. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: they report that EVE consistently outperformed Adam on the two datasets and attribute enhanced learning to dual learning rates and dual momentum terms. Their experiments do not separately isolate the contributions of those components.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes EVE and compares it with Adam; it does not reproduce the optimizer comparisons in V4 against SGD or momentum SGD.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report varying learning rates for both datasets; they describe EVE as consistently better than Adam across settings. The reported metrics are validation loss summaries for CIFAR-100 and figure-only validation loss/F1 for Flower Classification.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-100 with ResNet-50 trained for 25 epochs, EVE has lower reported validation-loss median, mean, standard deviation, and minimum than Adam: 3.37 versus 3.73, 4.20 versus 251.93, 7.18 versus 3,833.71, and 2.21 versus 2.55.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EVE can yield lower validation loss and less variable validation-loss trajectories than Adam in the tested learning-rate settings.

fits_no_version.finding: For DenseNet-201 on Flower Classification over 25 epochs, Section 4.2.4 reports better validation loss and Macro F1 for EVE than Adam across the tested learning-rate combinations; the supplied text gives no numeric figure values.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EVE can outperform Adam on held-out image-classification metrics in the tested settings.

record.problems: The optimizer comparison is only Adam versus the proposed EVE, not SGD or momentum SGD. CIFAR-100 validation results are aggregated across learning-rate settings; Flower validation results are described in figures without numeric values. The paper reports 25 epochs and does not state repeated-run uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately reported results that directly test the claim versions were identified. Training-loss and training-F1 comparisons do not measure held-out generalization and are not included as rows.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive methods versus SGD or momentum SGD; effects of tuning breadth, decoupled weight decay, or switching optimizers; language-model comparisons.
Effects of batch size under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Effects of adding or removing dropout and weight decay.
Association between magnitude-aware sharpness and generalization gaps, including comparisons with other measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The absence of an SGD comparator makes these results outside V4, rather than evidence that limits or challenges it. The reported standard deviations summarize validation losses; they are not identified as uncertainty across independent repeated runs.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same architectures and recipes.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers beyond Adam and EVE; broad versus limited tuning; SGD and momentum comparisons; language benchmarks; switching optimizers and decoupled weight decay.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptation to large batches.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Train with Adam on CIFAR-100 across the stated learning-rate settings; validation loss summarized across settings.
rows.measure: Validation loss median, mean, standard deviation, and minimum
rows.note: Adam's validation loss is compared with EVE's. The paper does not report a comparison with SGD or an error-gap measure.
rows.check: The Table 1 values are transcribed correctly, but Adam's validation loss alone cannot establish V4. The table does not specify precisely how observations across learning rates and epochs were pooled.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Train with EVE on CIFAR-100 across the stated learning-rate settings; validation loss summarized across settings.
rows.measure: Validation loss median, mean, standard deviation, and minimum
rows.note: EVE has lower reported validation-loss statistics than Adam, but V4 concerns adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD, which this comparison does not test.
rows.check: The values and Adam baseline match Table 1. EVE versus Adam compares two adaptive methods and cannot establish V4.

rows.subject: DenseNet-201

rows.measure: Validation loss and validation Macro F1-score
rows.note: The text says EVE outperforms Adam on validation metrics, but gives no numeric values for these figures.
rows.check: Adam's validation trajectories provide no SGD or momentum SGD comparison. Numeric figure values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

rows.subject: DenseNet-201

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The paper discusses optimizer generalization but reports no results testing the catalog's versions.

tranche.reason: EVE versus Adam compares two adaptive optimizers without an SGD or momentum SGD comparison. No claim version is tested or used as a tool.
